Escalate when any of the following holds: (1) two or more peripherals fail at the same time while the base station is online; (2) a firmware or protocol mismatch remains after an OTA attempt or OTA is not possible; (3) the standard frontline fix was executed and the problem persists; (4) the app's device list and the base station binding table disagree; (5) a device fails even next to the base station after a factory reset.

complaint: My kitchen camera disappeared this morning. It says offline. I already unplugged it and plugged it back in, tried a different power socket, and even restarted my Wi-Fi router because I assumed that is what the camera uses. The garden camera and the door sensor are fine, which is why I'm confused. The kitchen camera is the oldest one I own.
usability_reason: The response is clear and polite, and it correctly identifies a plausible root cause with supporting indicators. However, actionability is weak: the customer reply only says engineering will investigate and follow up, with no concrete next steps or timeline. Also, the session record shows no questions asked and no actions performed, yet the response presents detailed diagnostic findings (logs, error codes, firmware versions) as if checks were completed—these claims are not supported by the session record. It avoids claiming a fix was completed, which is good, but the unsupported diagnostic claims and lack of actionable guidance limit the score.
